title: Seth Rollins Explains How MITB Cash-In Saved Roman Reigns, Still Questioned About Shield Betrayal - NewsBreak
text:
By Sap Sinha ,
1 hours ago
Seth Rollins says Roman Reigns’ rough fan reaction in 2015 helped push his famous WrestleMania 31 Money in the Bank cash-in idea over the line.
During a recent interview with ESPN , Rollins explained that he had already suggested cashing in during the main event months before the show. However, when Reigns won the Royal Rumble in Philadelphia to loud boos, Rollins worried that a straight babyface coronation at WrestleMania would hurt Reigns’ first big title win.
As the main event with Brock Lesnar went long, Rollins sat in Gorilla position and feared that time was running out, thinking they might have to save the cash-in for RAW the next night instead. He finally got the signal, sprinted to the ring and pulled off The Heist of the Century, which he now considers the most iconic night of his career and the moment that made him a true singles star.
Rollins also admitted that even though he can play a babyface, he believes that he is much better as a heel. The Visionary claims that he is not very good at being the hero and cannot do it in long runs like John Cena or Rey Mysterio.

Rollins explained that he gets bored of himself in that role and thinks fans do too, which is why he feels more natural when he is playing a villain. Many of his favorite career memories involve him being a notorious heel, including his 2015 WWE Championship run after his WrestleMania 31 cash-in. Rollins noted that he can still step into the babyface role when needed, but in his mind his best and most comfortable work comes when he gives people a reason to boo.
The former WWE World Heavyweight Champion also revealed that Bobby Roode was the person who came up with the key crutch-drop visual during his recent SummerSlam Money in the Bank cash-in. Rollins noted that he did not rehearse with the crutches at all as WWE wanted to keep the surprise from leaking while CM Punk and GUNTHER were preparing their match.
When the time came, Rollins walked out selling a leg injury, then smoothly dropped the crutches to show that he was fine before attacking and cashing in on the tired champions. The dramatic spot, including the clean crutch drop, jacket removal and briefcase handoff, went better than he expected and helped cap off Punk and GUNTHER’s hard-hitting match. Rollins also admitted that there is pressure whenever he cashes in again as fans always compare everything to WrestleMania 31, but he feels the story with Punk made this moment stand on its own.
And finally, Rollins claims that WWE fans still confront him about breaking up The Shield more than a decade after the heel turn. Looking back on his WWE career, Rollins said that he, Roman Reigns and Dean Ambrose (Jon Moxley) did not fully grasp how big the betrayal would become when he first swung the steel chair in 2014.
Rollins recalled the crowd reaction as stunned silence rather than loud boos, because fans could not believe he was attacking his partners just after their big wins over Evolution. The moment sent him into The Authority and helped shape Reigns’ rise, but it also created a lasting bond in fans’ minds between himself, Reigns and that chair shot.
Rollins still hears people ask why he betrayed The Shield, and he is amazed that one turn has remained such a strong reference point for an entire generation of WWE fans.
summary: Seth Rollins says Roman Reigns’ rough fan reaction in 2015 helped push his famous WrestleMania 31 Money in the Bank cash-in idea over the line. As the main event with Brock Lesnar went long, Rollins sat in Gorilla position and feared that time was running out, thinking they might have to save the cash-in for RAW the next night instead. The former WWE World Heavyweight Champion also revealed that Bobby Roode was the person who came up with the key crutch-drop visual during his recent SummerSlam Money in the Bank cash-in.
